headline: US has effectively blocked Iranian oil exports at Hormuz
dek: Rubio: over the last 10-30 days about 13-14M barrels/day of oil move through Hormuz to global markets, 'some days equivalent to pre-conflict'; US military escorts and defends ships against Iranian attacks; Washington is blocking Iranian oil exports via sanctions + counterblockade; Iran has 'lost…
sources: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Breitbart News interview Oct 15, released by the State Department Oct 19
fault_line: Whose blockade is it? Washington: 'we escort 13M barrels/day, Iran ships nothing.' Tehran: 'we manage the strait, violating tankers burn.' Both claim control of the same water on the same day.

sections.what_happened: Rubio: over the last 10-30 days about 13-14M barrels/day of oil move through Hormuz to global markets, 'some days equivalent to pre-conflict'; US military escorts and defends ships against Iranian attacks; Washington is blocking Iranian oil exports via sanctions + counterblockade; Iran has 'lost control of the waterway' after US operations.
sections.what_verified: IANS/asiaPOST with direct quotes; consistent with Chris Wright's '80% of prewar flows' (Fox News). State Dept released the interview.
sections.what_disputed: asiaPOST itself notes figures are the administration's assessment, not independently verified; directly contradicts Iran's claim of sovereign control/management of the strait and IRGC's tanker-mining claims on the same day; Israel/US 'economic blockade' framing contested by Tehran and Moscow (Araghchi-Lavrov presser).
sections.why_matters: Pair with 1500-01: two mutually exclusive claims of control over the world's most important oil lane, both issued within 24 hours. TOTW does the split, not the bloc — show Rubio's numbers and the IRGC's statement side by side, with what each side can't prove.
sections.context: Background: Rubio: US has effectively blocked Iranian oil exports at Hormuz; 13-14M bbl/day transiting under US escort; 'the only country that cannot get a single barrel through is Iran'

totw_analysis: Our read: Pair with 1500-01: two mutually exclusive claims of control over the world's most important oil lane, both issued within 24 hours. TOTW does the split, not the bloc — show Rubio's numbers and the IRGC's statement side by side, with what each side can't prove. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Whose blockade is it? Washington: 'we escort 13M barrels/day, Iran ships nothing.' Tehran: 'we manage the strait, violating tankers burn.' Both claim control of the same water on the same day.
